name: Crunchies
summary: Golden oat and coconut bars sweetened with golden syrup, crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle, the tin-cupboard bake of South African homes.
about: Crunchies are a South African baking classic: oats, coconut and flour bound with butter and golden syrup, baked in a tray and cut into squares. They keep for weeks in an airtight tin, which is why they turn up in lunch boxes, bake sales, road-trip padkos and church fêtes.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Grease a baking tray of about 30 × 20 cm and line it with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a pot over medium heat until bubbling, about 3 minutes. Take it off the heat and stir in the bicarbonate of soda; it will foam up and turn pale.
Pour the foaming butter into the dry ingredients straight away and stir until every oat is coated.
Tip into the tray and press down firmly and evenly with the back of a metal spoon.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until evenly golden brown all over; it will still feel soft but firms as it cools.
Cut into 24 squares while still warm, then leave in the tray until completely cool and crisp, about 30 minutes, before lifting them out.
prepNote: Keeps up to 2 weeks in an airtight tin.
